sources.entry: OneClip - A simple and professional macOS clipboard manager. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Wcowin/OneClip) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: OneClip is a native SwiftUI clipboard manager for macOS that keeps a searchable history of copied text, images and files, with extras like a stack clipboard, drag container, quick reply templates, OCR and AI summarization.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs in the menu bar and automatically saves clipboard history for text, images, files and other formats, stored locally in SQLite. Users can search history with highlighting, pin, favorite, edit and delete items, and browse in list or card views. Hotkey-driven panels include a stack clipboard for batch paste, a drag container for staging files to drop into other apps, quick reply templates, and a quick-paste panel. Other features listed are screenshots, OCR, selection and screenshot translation, a JS scripting system, AI integration with local Ollama/LM Studio or online services, LAN sync between devices, a URL Scheme API, and Finder cut-and-paste file moves. The README says the current official release is commercial, while the early open-source version in the src/ directory is MIT-licensed and file-system based.
use_cases: Keep a searchable history of everything I copied on my Mac
Paste multiple copied items in sequence when filling forms
Stage files or images and drag them into other apps
Store and insert reusable text, image or file reply templates
Extract text from screenshots or images with OCR
Summarize or translate clipboard content with a local or online AI
how_to_run: Or download OneClip.app from the GitHub Releases page and move it to Applications
Grant Accessibility permission in System Settings (required)
Build the early open-source version: git clone the repo, cd OneClip/src, chmod +x build.sh, ./build.sh
Run the built app: open dist/OneClip.app
notable: Stack clipboard: batch-collect items and paste them one by one with Cmd+V
Drag container for temporarily holding files and images before dropping them into other apps
Finder cut (Cmd+X) and paste (Cmd+V) to move files, which the README says is free here
Early source code is MIT-licensed and published in src/, while the current release is commercial
caveats: Accessibility permission is required, and full disk access is needed for some file operations
The open-source code is an early, file-system-based version; the current official version is commercial and closed-source, with a 7-day trial for full features
Unsigned builds may need the quarantine attribute removed via terminal on first launch
summary.license: MIT for the early open-source src/ code; the README states the current official release is commercial
